claims.text: Setting the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
The `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service specifies the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API (for example `tf.pulumiapi.acmecorp.com`).
When `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is unset on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
The DNS record for the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` domain should point at the same host that serves `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN` in a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud deployment.

In self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, a separate domain for the Terraform-compatible API is not required: `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` can be set to the same value as `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN`, so no second DNS record is needed.

The Terraform/OpenTofu state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the domain in the Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.
A page exists at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ documenting the Terraform state backend guide for Pulumi Cloud.
For a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name, `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration use the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` value as the hostname.
Both Terraform and OpenTofu can use Pulumi Cloud as a state backend (via the Terraform-compatible API).
